newsitem.title: USA: Tender accepted for Robbins, Il. incinerator bonds.
newsitem.headline: Tender accepted for Robbins, Il. incinerator bonds.

text.p: A tender offer for $320 million of bonds sold by Robbins, Ill., to finance a waste-to-energy incinerator has been accepted, Foster Wheeler Corp said Tuesday.
The tender, which began Sept 18 and ended Monday, resulted in 99.9 percent of the resource recovery revenue bonds being tendered, the company said in a release.
The exchange of restructured bonds is scheduled to take place Oct 15 in Chicago, according to the release.
When completed later this year, the plant will be operated by Robbins Resource Recovery Partners L.P., a subsidiary of Foster Wheeler of Clinton, N.J.

As a result of the exchange, restructured bonds in the amount of nearly $320 million consisting of $234 million of series 1994A bonds and $85 million of series 1994B bonds will be issued, while existing series 1994A bonds in the amount of $250,000 will remain outstanding.
The restructured bonds will have additional credit support, the benefit of additional covenants, different redemption provisions, a lower interest rate and, in some cases, extended maturity dates.
The bond restructuring, which was announced in May, followed the elimination of a state of Illinois subsidy for the Robbins incinerator and two other bond-financed incinerators in the state.
A lawsuit filed by Foster Wheeler against state officials challenging the lost subsidy is pending in U.S. District Court in Chicago.
A ruling on the state's motion to dismiss the lawsuit on constitutional grounds is expected Oct 23.
